purpose: Where each AC-11 axis envelope comes from, so a CI lane can assemble the aggregator's manifest instead of a person assembling it by hand. tools/aggregate_ac11_evidence.py has never been run by CI (48-task rescore v1.8 §4-5-3), which is why its recomputed PASS count is 0/8 -- not because the axes fail, but because nothing calls it. This file is the input that makes calling it possible, and it is deliberately honest about the axes that have no measurement means yet: naming them here with the reason is what keeps the aggregator's INVALID_RUN legible instead of mysterious.
note: chain is the measured state of the producer -> workflow -> importer path, read from the tree rather than asserted -- and 'the importer exists' is not the same as 'the importer emits an axis envelope', which is the mistake r1 caught. envelopeShape records what the importer actually writes: 'axis-evidence' is one envelope, 'axes-bundle' is a wrapper whose axes array holds them, and 'not-an-axis-envelope' means the importer's output cannot go into the aggregator at all. 'complete' therefore requires producer, workflow, importer AND an admissible shape. The aggregator requires all eight envelopes and refuses otherwise, so an incomplete or absent axis makes the run INVALID_RUN by design -- that is the fail-closed answer, and the reason text is what tells the reader what is in the way. importerEmitsAxes is read from the importer file as an EXACT set, not as a subset: r1 only checked that each claimed name appears somewhere, so a migration row naming one of its two axes stayed true while describing half the chain (#299 r2). A row with no importer emits nothing, so its set is empty however much its producer names. Card 216 closed the security chain: the importer now adapts the producer's report into an axis envelope (runPurpose ac11-axis-evidence, the reviewed target registry, the artifact digests it already measured), so the chain is complete in the sense this file means -- an admissible envelope exists. The axis still does not pass, for a different and narrower reason: the aggregator requires four threat reports and only SEC-SCAN-001 has a producer anywhere in this repository, so the envelope's verdict is NOT_OBSERVED and names the three that are missing. 'complete' is about the chain, not about the verdict. Measured at 097da87d with the real run 36943527856: the assembler now puts this axis into the manifest (assembledAxes names it for the first time) and the aggregator evaluates it instead of reporting it missing. It still refuses the envelope, with a narrower reason that belongs to the producer rather than the adapter -- 'environment.comparableGroup is required', which the security producer does not write. An adapter must not invent a comparability group: whether two runs are comparable is a property of how they were produced.
